# Unit test for function words_string
def test_words_string():
    # Empty string returns empty list
    assert words_string("") == []

    # None input returns empty list
    assert words_string(None) == []

    # Single word with no separators
    assert words_string("hello") == ["hello"]

    # Words separated by spaces
    assert words_string("hello world foo") == ["hello", "world", "foo"]

    # Words separated by commas
    assert words_string("hello,world,foo") == ["hello", "world", "foo"]

    # Mixed commas and spaces
    assert words_string("Hi, my name is John") == ["Hi", "my", "name", "is", "John"]

    # Classic example from spec
    assert words_string("One, two, three, four, five, six") == ["One", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six"]

    # Consecutive commas collapse into whitespace
    assert words_string("One,, two, three") == ["One", "two", "three"]

    # String with only commas/spaces yields empty list
    assert words_string(" , , ") == []

    # Comma-separated with no spaces
    assert words_string("One,two,three,four,five") == ["One", "two", "three", "four", "five"]

    # Leading/trailing separators are ignored by split()
    assert words_string(",start middle end,") == ["start", "middle", "end"]
